newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, nearbys up with corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, nearbys up with corn, soy.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby months firm on a rally in corn and soybean futures with news India has halted wheat exports also viewed as supportive, traders said.
Deferred months ended lower on bull spreading with good wheat seeding weather in U.S. winter wheat growing regions also weighing on the new crop July, they said.
Bombay traders Friday said Indian wheat exports had ground to a halt as a state agency had not issued export licenses due to a shortage of government-owned supplies.
"There have been no wheat exports since September 30," a Bombay-based foodgrains exporter.
But some traders were skeptical of the Indian news.
Many market watchers said trading in wheat was very quiet and gave a nod to corn and soybeans as Monday's floor leader.
"I think most of the strength came out of corn and beans and they aren't exactly putting on a stellar performance," a trader said.
Corn and soybeans closed higher Monday on a technical bounce from an oversold condition.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher to three cents lower, with December up 1-1/2 at $4.22-1/2.

Continental Grain bull spread one million bushels of March/July and was a net buyer of one million March, traders said. Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp sold 1.5 million December and The Chicago Corp sold one million December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 17,788 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 200 March $4.30 calls at 11 cents and USA Trading sold 200 March $4.30 calls at 12 to 12-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,800 contracts, down from 7,940 Friday.
